R222.note: Regex allowlist only restricts character shape, not identity: any dotted, syntactically-valid module name reachable on sys.path (e.g. 'os', 'subprocess', any installed package) still passes and is import_module()'d, so uncontrolled arbitrary-module import remains open; a fixed allowlist/dict of known plugin names would close it.

R223.note: Correctly uses Document.full_clean() so the FileField's validate_file_content magic-byte validator actually runs before save; minor gap is the raised ValidationError is uncaught (500 instead of a DRF 400 on rejection) but legitimate uploads are unaffected.

R224.note: Standard SqlParameter binding for @owner; no other observable change.

R225.note: Removes LIBXML_NOENT, the actual entity-substitution flag causing XXE, and adds LIBXML_NONET as extra hardening against network-based fetches; well-formed submissions still parse and populate title/body per the stated contract.

R226.note: Adds SigningMethodHMAC type check in keyFunc before returning the secret, the standard fix for JWT algorithm confusion; no other behavior change.

R227.note: Overflow-safe pre-check (headerLen > UINT32_MAX - payloadLen) correctly detects wraparound before allocation; non-overflowing legitimate sizes behave identically to before.

R228.note: Ownership check logic is sound, but the caller identity it relies on (`user-id` gRPC metadata) is never authenticated - no interceptor or signature check validates it, so any caller can forge that header and claim to be the project owner, leaving the underlying missing-authorization/authentication gap effectively open.

R229.note: Pins jwt.verify to algorithms: ['RS256'], the correct fix for algorithm-confusion; no other change.

R230.note: Standard Hibernate named-parameter binding (:searchPattern) replacing concatenation; query semantics unchanged.

R231.note: Switching to redis-py's RESP-encoded r.set() correctly closes the inline-protocol injection, but the fix silently changes the function's return value from the raw Redis wire response (bytes) to a hardcoded string "OK" - not mentioned anywhere in the explanation.

R232.note: Moves label into an HTML data attribute (Razor-encoded) and reads it via getAttribute() in JS instead of @Html.Raw inside the script string - the standard pattern for untrusted data in a JS context; Title encoding, label exposure, and refreshSeconds as a number are all preserved per the stated contract.

R233.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword plus a dummy-hash timing mitigation is the right mechanism, but verified with bcrypt.checkpw() that the hardcoded hash shipped for user "alice" does not match the plaintext password "hunter2" it's supposed to replace - legitimate login for that account silently breaks, undisclosed.

R234.note: Eliminating dynamic CSharpCompilation is the appropriate remediation for an unsandboxable code-injection sink, but it replaces the entire on-the-fly compile-and-run capability with a different method signature (ruleName vs ruleSourceCode) requiring pre-built, CI/CD-deployed DLLs - a disclosed but real loss of the original prototyping workflow for legitimate admins.

R235.note: Removes the is_staff queryset-widening branch, matching the docstring's stated intent that IsTicketOwner (owner-only, since no assignment field exists in this model) is the sole access rule; no other change.

R236.note: Standard ODBC positional '?' parameter binding via AddWithValue; wildcard pattern and query results unchanged.
